o.text: From Arabic تَقْدِيمَات (taqdīmāt). By surface analysis, təqdim + -at.
From Classical Persian بتپرست. By surface analysis, büt + -pərəst
From birləş- + -mə. Most senses have likely been semantically influenced by Russian объединение (obʺjedinenije)/соединение (sojedinenije).

Present participle compound of od (“fire”) + saçmaq (“to throw, to shed”).
Likely a calque of Russian огнемёт (ognemjót). Compare Uzbek oʻtsochar and Kazakh отшашар (otšašar).
